newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London firm on Tokyo's gains.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London firm on Tokyo's gains.

text.p: Japanese shares were slightly firmer following Tokyo's better performance on Tuesday but trade was thin ahead of the Japanese financial year-end on March 31, traders said.

Nomura Securities remained weak after news that its head office in Japan had been raided by prosecutors and securities markets officials who were investigating alleged illegal payments to "sokaiya", or corporate racketeers.

"I think people were largely expecting it in Tokyo, it's just another string to the bow really and I think people are now waiting to see what measures they (the Japanese authorities) come up with," one trader said.
The Nikkei/ISE 50 share index was up 13.20 points from Monday's London close, or 0.93 percent higher at 1,436.08.
The Nikkei-225 closed up 395.79 points, or 2.19 percent, at 18,439.61.
Nomura, which dropped 20 yen to 1,440 in Tokyo, was trading at 1,431 yen by in London by 1555 GMT.
Elsewhere, Sony Corp was at 8,455 yen in London compared with its close of 8,410 in Tokyo and Fujitsu Ltd was at 1,252-1/2 yen versus a Tokyo finish of 1,250.
